cards.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Meetings for Workplace
cards.body: Claude can now draft plans during discussions, map timelines on whiteboards, answer meeting chat questions, and access connected work apps. The AI assistant transforms real-time conversations into actionable tasks and documentation.

cards.title: Google Expands AI Chip Portfolio with New TPUs
cards.body: Google launched specialized tensor processing units designed for confidential model training and increased memory capacity. The new chips broaden Google's AI hardware offerings across more use cases.

cards.title: Meta's Muse AI Agent Reaches Smartwatches
cards.body: Meta's AI assistant is now available on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS through voice calls, text messages, and dictation. Users can interact with Muse directly from their wrists.

cards.title: Adobe Adds AI Agents to Creative Suite
cards.body: Adobe integrated AI agents into Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly with new creative tools. The company launched a prototype builder in Firefly to compete with Figma.

cards.title: Anthropic Sets IPO Price Range at $70-78
cards.body: Anthropic's IPO valuation could reach $1.404 trillion at the top of its price range on a fully diluted basis. The company is moving forward with its public offering plans.

cards.title: Spotify's AI DJ Gets New Voices
cards.body: Spotify Premium users can now customize their AI DJ with different voice personalities and adjust commentary levels. The feature allows users to reduce chatter between songs.

cards.title: Cyanogen Co-Founder Launches Kora OS
cards.body: Kora is a free-to-use alternative to Windows targeting AI-heavy users and developers. The new operating system is designed for the AI era with native agent support.

cards.title: Ring Launches Security Drone and Robot
cards.body: Amazon's Ring expanded into robotics with a home security drone and enterprise patrol robot. The new devices enhance residential and business security capabilities.

cards.title: Cyberattacks Threaten Open Source AI Security
cards.body: Hugging Face warns that rising cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force stricter security measures. Increased restrictions may compromise the accessibility that defines open-source communities.

cards.title: Otter AI Supports 30+ Languages Now
cards.body: Otter AI expanded language support to 27 additional languages with multilingual detection capabilities. The platform can now follow conversations when speakers switch between languages.

cards.title: Anthropic Plans IPO Valuation Announcement
cards.body: Anthropic is expected to announce its IPO valuation range this week. The AI company continues moving forward with its public offering timeline.

cards.title: Jensen Huang Hired PR Firm Over Year Ago
cards.body: Nvidia's CEO engaged a PR firm specializing in high-profile scandals approximately one year prior to recent controversies. The firm was hired shortly after initial New York Times reporting.

cards.title: Short Seller Warned of Huang Connections
cards.body: Culper Research flagged Jensen Huang's suspicious relationship with a Chinese executive six months before the scandal erupted. The short seller had questioned these ties earlier this year.

cards.title: Securities Lawsuits Target Nvidia Board
cards.body: Nvidia's stock fell 4% after the board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's connections. Legal experts warn Nvidia's earlier statements could create costly liability.

cards.title: Jensen Huang Cancels Public Speaking Events
cards.body: Nvidia's CEO withdrew from the ElevenLabs Summit and an Anthropic event amid ongoing controversies. Huang is reducing his public appearances during the investigation period.

cards.title: Anthropic Releases Mythos and Fable Models
cards.body: Anthropic launched new models showing improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision capabilities. The models also communicate more clearly with users than predecessors.

cards.title: Huang Scandal Threatens Nvidia's China Strategy
cards.body: Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy complicates Nvidia's efforts to loosen chip export restrictions. The controversy jeopardizes the company's access to China's AI market.

cards.title: Meta Releases Muse Ember Lightweight Model
cards.body: Meta's new Ember model costs 10 cents per million input tokens, undercutting frontier competitors significantly. The lightweight model is designed for efficient agent execution.

cards.title: Anthropic Buys $3.4B in Natural Gas Turbines
cards.body: Anthropic invested billions in natural gas turbines to power AI infrastructure. The massive energy purchase reflects the company's commitment to scaling computational capacity.

cards.title: Pelosi's Successor Targets AI and Data Centers
cards.body: California state senator Scott Wiener, who authored AI regulation legislation, won Nancy Pelosi's congressional seat and could shape federal AI policy. His appointment signals a shift toward stricter governance of advanced AI technologies.

cards.title: Data Center Power Demands Drive Electricity Debate
cards.body: The backlash against data center expansion is fundamentally rooted in electricity concerns, not data center technology itself. As AI infrastructure grows, energy availability becomes the limiting factor for further buildout.

cards.title: Nancy Pelosi's Replacement Ready to Regulate AI
cards.body: Scott Wiener authored legislation to curb advanced AI risks as a California state senator. Now in Congress, he's positioned to play a key role in setting federal AI policy.

cards.title: The Climate Case for AI Remains Unproven
cards.body: As UN climate conference delegates meet, AI's climate benefits are being challenged by experts. The case for AI as a climate solution has not been convincingly made.

cards.title: AI Innovation Requires Reliable Data and Expertise
cards.body: Specialty chemicals companies face a key challenge: connecting new AI and advanced modeling technologies to reliable data and scientific expertise. Bridging this gap is essential for bringing AI-enhanced products to market.

cards.title: Humanoid Robots Begin Entering Consumer Services
cards.body: A new humanoid robot cleaning service launched in San Francisco, offering a glimpse of AI-powered robotics in everyday life. The experience suggests autonomous humanoids may soon become practical tools for household services.

cards.title: Texas AI Data Center Boom Shows Signs of Collapse
cards.body: Texas became the fastest-growing data center market in the US, but this momentum may be faltering. Energy policy shifts and infrastructure challenges are threatening the state's position as an AI hub.

cards.title: DeepMind Releases Gemini Robotics 2.5
cards.body: DeepMind unveiled Gemini Robotics 2.5, advancing AI capabilities for robotic systems. The release includes an open safety benchmark called ASIMOV-jailbreak for testing AI model robustness.

cards.title: Nvidia Faces Leadership Succession Challenges
cards.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's dominance has created a significant leadership vacuum with no obvious successor in sight. The company's future stability depends on addressing this organizational vulnerability.

cards.title: Ukraine's Fiber-Optic Drones Caught in AI Competition
cards.body: AI data center demand is squeezing resources for Ukraine's fiber-optic drone technology development. The competition for manufacturing capacity highlights the growing resource constraints amid AI's rapid expansion.

cards.title: Claude AI Code Exposing Secrets on GitHub
cards.body: Claude Code is accidentally leaking sensitive information and secrets across GitHub repositories. The vulnerability highlights security risks in AI-assisted coding tools.

cards.title: Sam Altman Parody Demonstrates Memory Management Flaw
cards.body: A humorous Sam Altman parody inadvertently exposed an important lesson in AI memory management. The incident illustrates how AI systems can fail in unexpected ways through simple mistakes.
